Target audience: High school students or math enthusiasts

Section: section_1 — The Hook: A Counter-Intuitive Challenge

Lecture lines:
Can two blocks counting collisions find Pi?
Small mass moves toward a giant wall block.
Collisions occur between these two blocks.
The counts match Pi's first digits!
Let's reveal how this simple math works.

Planned animations:
Display a single square hitting a wall. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Show a second square colliding with the first. (Color: #FF0000)
Simulate the chaos of multiple collisions. (Color: #00FF00)

Section: section_2 — Prerequisites: Conservation of Momentum and Energy

Lecture lines:
Collisions conserve both momentum and kinetic energy.
Mapping velocities creates a 2D configuration space.
This point moves steadily along the trajectory.

Planned animations:
Show momentum vector p = mv. (Color: #00FFFF)
Visualize kinetic energy E = 1/2mv^2. (Color: #FFFF00)
Compare both formulas in grid layout. (Color: #FFFFFF)

Section: section_3 — Mapping Collisions to Geometry

Lecture lines:
Energy conservation defines a circle boundary.
Collisions act as reflections in a wedge.
Total collisions equal reflections in this wedge.
Wedge angles are dictated by mass ratios.
Geometry transforms physics into a count.

Planned animations:
Draw a trajectory line on a coordinate plane. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Highlight collision point as a reflection. (Color: #FF00FF)
Show the path changing angle. (Color: #00FFFF)

Section: section_4 — The Emergence of Pi

Lecture lines:
Heavier mass reduces the wedge angle.
The path length approximates the arc length.
The ratio relates directly to Pi.
This is the emergence of Pi.
The geometry forces the numerical count.

Planned animations:
Display Pi symbol in center. (Color: #FF9900)
Show square digits converging to Pi. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Highlight the digits as they form. (Color: #FFFF00)

Section: section_5 — Conclusion and Intuition Check

Lecture lines:
Counting bounces reveals Pi's hidden digits.
Discrete collisions meet continuous geometric curves.
Physics encodes Pi in simple motion.

Planned animations:
Review the key collision steps. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Summarize the emergence of Pi. (Color: #FF9900)
Final display of the core concept. (Color: #00FF00)

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Intuition Check", [
            "Counting bounces reveals Pi's hidden digits.",

        self.play(FadeIn(table))

        )

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(2)
